milestones.title: M1 — Content-Powered Website Shell
milestones.goal: Create the initial repository, local structured content foundation, and Next.js website shell so the site renders real profile identity content from src/content instead of hardcoded page text.
scope: Create the my-website-2026 repository structure.
Create local structured content files under src/content.
Create the Next.js personal website app structure.
Render profile/site identity data from src/content/profile.ts and src/content/links.ts.
Implement the shared layout shell: root layout, page container, top navigation, footer, and homepage hero placeholder.
Add docs/DESIGN.md and the generated project documentation scaffold.
Wire the homepage hero to local content so the displayed name, positioning statement, and primary links come from structured content files.
deliverables: Homepage shell rendering local profile data.
Initial docs folder with project overview, roadmap, workflows, project tree, and milestones.
successCriteria: The website builds successfully.
The homepage displays Dai Le's identity from local structured content.
No profile identity text is duplicated directly in the website page component.
The repo has a stable src/app, src/components, src/content, src/lib, docs, public, scripts, tests structure.
The first visible page already looks like the beginning of the final website, not a throwaway scaffold.

milestones.title: M2 — Dual-Mode Premium Theme
milestones.goal: Implement the light/dark visual system as a complete user-facing feature, including theme state, persistence, accessible toggle UI, and design-token-driven surfaces.
scope: Add CSS variables for soft grey light mode and charcoal grey dark mode.
Add violet/cyan accent tokens, text tokens, border tokens, card tokens, and focus tokens.
Create ThemeProvider and ThemeToggle components.
Persist selected theme in local storage or an equivalent browser-safe preference layer.
Respect system preference before the user selects a manual theme.
Wire the theme toggle into the navigation.
Apply theme tokens to the app shell, homepage hero, navigation, footer, cards, buttons, and links.
deliverables: Light mode using soft grey, not pure white.
Dark mode using charcoal grey, not pure black.
successCriteria: Users can switch between light and dark mode.
The theme choice persists after reload.
Theme switching does not cause layout shift.
Light mode is visibly grey rather than white.
Dark mode is visibly charcoal rather than black.
The theme toggle is keyboard accessible and has an accessible label.

milestones.goal: Ship the Work page as a complete feature that renders selected project cards from local structured project content.
scope: Add project types and project records to src/content/projects.ts.
Add project fields for title, slug, summary, status, role, stack, links, featured flag, and display priority.
Create website content adapters for projects.
Create reusable ProjectCard and ProjectGrid components.
Build the /work page using local structured project data.
Add project links for GitHub, demo, case study, product page, or roadmap where available.
Add unique SEO metadata for /work.
deliverables: Featured and standard project card layouts.
successCriteria: The /work page renders selected projects from local structured content.
Each project card has a clear title, summary, status, stack, and useful links.
Featured projects are visually prioritized.
No project card content is duplicated in page components.
The page works in both themes and across mobile, tablet, and desktop layouts.

milestones.goal: Ship the my-dev-kit Ecosystem product page as one connected product-family feature covering my-dev-kit, my-dev-kit-orchestrator, and my-dev-kit-lab.
scope: Add product-family types to local content.
Add my-dev-kit Ecosystem content as one product family.
Add module records for my-dev-kit, my-dev-kit-orchestrator, and my-dev-kit-lab.
Describe the ecosystem as Codebase Intelligence -> Workflow Orchestration -> Validation Lab.
Create ProductFamilyHero, EcosystemModuleCard, and EcosystemDiagram components.
Build /products/my-dev-kit using local ecosystem content.
Add GitHub/package/docs links for each module where available.
Add unique SEO metadata for the ecosystem page.

The page does not make the projects look like unrelated GitHub repos.

The page looks premium and technical in both light and dark mode.

Add roadmap data to src/content/roadmaps.ts.
Support suite-level roadmaps and project-level roadmap lanes.
Support statuses: shipped, active, planned, exploring, paused, and deferred.
Add updatedAt, summary, phases, lanes, milestones, links, and display priority fields.
Add my-dev-kit Ecosystem roadmap with lanes for my-dev-kit, my-dev-kit-orchestrator, and my-dev-kit-lab.
Create website adapters for roadmap data.
Create RoadmapPreview, RoadmapShowcase, RoadmapTimeline, RoadmapPhaseCard, RoadmapStatusBadge, RoadmapMilestoneList, RoadmapProgressRail, and RoadmapUpdatedLabel.
Render the full roadmap on /products/my-dev-kit.
Render a compact roadmap preview on the homepage or product preview section.
successCriteria: Roadmaps render from local structured content, not duplicated markdown.
The roadmap looks like a premium product strategy dashboard, not a plain bullet list.
The full roadmap works on desktop and mobile.
Statuses are communicated with text, not color alone.
The roadmap is readable in light mode and dark mode.
The roadmap uses lightweight static/server-rendered content where possible.

milestones.goal: Ship the homepage as a polished landing page that combines identity, selected work, product lab previews, roadmap previews, publications, and contact CTAs.
scope: Wire homepage sections to local structured content.

The homepage remains fast and responsive.

milestones.title: M12 — Premium Visual Polish
milestones.goal: Ship the premium visual layer as a controlled feature that improves brand perception without hurting readability, accessibility, or performance.
scope: Add lightweight hero visual module.
Add subtle technical dashboard motifs.
Add radial glow and soft grid texture.
Add premium hover states for cards and buttons.
Add subtle roadmap rail and active-phase visual treatment.

successCriteria: The site feels more premium and product-like after the milestone.

Roadmaps remain readable.
Reduced-motion users are respected.
The site remains fast after the visual layer is added.

milestones.title: M13 — Responsive and Accessibility Hardening
milestones.goal: Ship the cross-device and accessibility hardening feature so the website feels consistent across devices, browsers, screen resolutions, input modes, and both themes.
scope: Audit and fix layouts at 360px, 390px, 768px, 1024px, 1280px, 1440px, and 1920px.
Fix unintended horizontal scrolling.
Fix card overflow, roadmap overflow, clipped text, and gallery distortion.
Harden mobile navigation.
Verify keyboard navigation.
Verify focus states.
Add or correct aria labels.
Verify semantic HTML structure.
Verify reduced-motion behavior.
Check light and dark mode contrast.
successCriteria: No unintended horizontal scrolling occurs at required viewport widths.
Navigation remains usable on mobile and desktop.
Roadmaps do not overflow on mobile.
Keyboard navigation works for navigation, theme toggle, cards, and CTAs.
Focus states are visible.
Status is never communicated by color alone.
The site feels like the same product across device sizes.

milestones.title: M14 — Performance and Release Readiness
milestones.goal: Ship the performance/release-readiness feature so the website is fast, production-safe, and ready for public deployment.
scope: Run production build and fix build errors.
Optimize images and media loading.
Lazy-load below-the-fold media.
Reduce unnecessary client components.
Avoid runtime roadmap parsing where static rendering is possible.
Analyze and reduce bundle size.
Optimize font loading.
Check for console errors.
Run Lighthouse or equivalent production checks.
Verify external links.
Finalize 404 page and deployment configuration.
Prepare GitHub and Vercel deployment readiness.
successCriteria: Production build succeeds.
No critical console errors remain.
Images are optimized and do not cause layout shift.
Roadmaps render efficiently from local structured content.
Lighthouse targets are acceptable for first public release.
All critical links work.
The site is ready to deploy as v1.0.0.
